title: Activating ... should reset the keyboard focus

labels.name: needs implementer interest
labels.description: Moving the issue forward requires implementers to express interest

labels.name: needs tests
labels.description: Moving the issue forward requires someone to write tests

body: Per https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/browsing-the-web.html#scroll-to-the-fragment-identifier, activating `...` does - scroll the page to #foo (step 3.2) - move sequential focus navigation starting point to #foo (step 3.5) This make sure that keyboard users are navigated to #foo. However, the activating `...` doesn't reset the keyboard focus while it scrolls the page (step 2.2). This causes that keyboard users aren't navigated to the top of the page. A keyboard user presses the tab key then the element next to `...` receives the focus (and the page will be scrolled to the element). I think that this is not fair. So I would like to add sub-steps to step 2 as follows: 1. If there is no indicated part of the document, set the Document's target element to null. 2. If the indicated part of the document is the top of the document, then: 1. Set the Document's target element to null. 2. Scroll to the beginning of the document for the Document. [CSSOMVIEW] 3. **Run the focusing steps for the Document's viewport.** 4. **Unset the sequential focus navigation starting point.** 3. Otherwise: 1. Let target be element that is the indicated part of the document. 2. Set the Document's target element to target. 3. Use the scroll an element into view algorithm to scroll target into view, with the align to top flag set. [CSSOMVIEW] 4. Run the focusing steps for target, with the Document's viewport as the fallback target. 5. Move the sequential focus navigation starting point to target. I think that sub-steps I added (2.3 and 2.4) reset the keyboard focus. Please let me know if they are wrong or there are better solutions. Note: As far as I know, no browsers reset the keyboard focus for #top as currently spec'd.
